title: Chunked file sync with a deadline budget
name: Chunked file uploader

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the overall time budget for a sync? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: remaining is computed as deadlineAt - startedAt, which always equals budgetMs and never shrinks as chunks upload. Each chunk therefore gets min(budget, 15s) regardless of elapsed time, so a sync of many slow chunks can run far beyond the client's deadline; the overrun is only noticed at commit (where Date.now() is used correctly), after all the work has been done. It should be deadlineAt - Date.now().

choiceQuestions.prompt: A 20 MB file is re-synced and all of its chunk hashes are already in knownChunks. What does the store see?
choices: Five putChunk calls followed by commitFile
Only a commitFile call listing all five chunks
Only a commitFile call with an empty chunk list
choiceQuestions.explanation: Every chunk is still hashed and pushed onto `chunks` before the existing.has check, then skipped. commitFile is always called with the full chunk list. No putChunk calls happen; the commit is not skipped; the list is not empty.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A putChunk call rejects with a network error before its timer fires. What does handleSync do?
choices: Returns 504 with stage set to that chunk
Rethrows the network error to its caller
Skips the chunk and continues with the next one
Retries the chunk until the budget is exhausted
choiceQuestions.explanation: withTimeout only converts errors into DeadlineExceededError when the signal was aborted. A network error with no abort is rethrown unchanged, and handleSync rethrows anything that is not a DeadlineExceededError. There is no skip or retry logic.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A client sends clientDeadlineMs = 900000. What budget does the sync run with?
choiceQuestions.explanation: handleSync clamps with Math.min(clientDeadlineMs, MAX_BUDGET_MS), giving 300000. 60000 is only the default when none is given, and 15000 is the per-chunk cap, not the budget.
